mofsl_2qfy27.headline: Strong Tier-2 growth offsets a mixed quarter for larger peers
mofsl_2qfy27.read: IT services median revenue growth was 2.3% QoQ CC in 2QFY27 (vs +1.2/+0.8/+1.6/+1.5% in 1QFY27/4QFY26/3QFY26/2QFY26). Tier-1 grew 1.2% QoQ CC (HCLT 2.3%, TechM 2.4%, Wipro 0.5%, TCS flat) while Tier-2 grew 3.0% (Persistent 7.8%, Zensar 4.1%, Mphasis 3.3%, Cyient 2.6%; Coforge 10.9% incl. 3.8% organic). Tier-1 EBIT margin fell 20bp YoY to 20.2% and Tier-2 stayed flat at 14.6%; TCV was uneven (Infosys +68%, HCLT +27%, TechM +25% YoY vs Wipro -45%, Coforge +102%, Mphasis -12%, KPIT -8%), with shrinking deal sizes raising Tier-1 vs Tier-2 competition. Guidance: Infosys cut FY27 organic guidance a second time to (-0.5%) to 0.5% CC; HCLT raised the low end of revenue growth to 2.5-4.0% and cut IT services guidance to 3-4%; LTM expects FY27 growth close to FY26's 5.3%; Coforge raised EBIT margin guidance to 16% (from 15.5%) with a USD2.4b order book (+45%); Mphasis raised growth to low double digits. No rating changes.

buoyant_skill: anthropic-skills:it-services-analysis (Buoyant already runs a live price-driver model for IT services in this app at /sector/it-services); anthropic-skills:erd-services-analysis for ER&D names
unit_economics: USD revenue = prior revenue x (1 + constant-currency growth) x cross-currency effect; EBIT = revenue - employee cost (headcount x cost per head, set by wage hike, utilisation and pyramid) - subcontracting - other costs - D&A; INR EBIT also moves with USD/INR (1% rupee depreciation adds ~20-30bp for IT services, ~50-60bp for ER&D per Buoyant working rules).

price_drivers.why: Tier-2 growth of 3.0% QoQ against Tier-1 at 1.2% in 2QFY27 explains why Persistent, Coforge and Zensar re-rate while Infosys, LTM and Hexaware lag on a second guidance cut.
TCV is the lead on revenue 2-4 quarters out; Coforge TCV +102% and a USD2.4b order book (+45%) support its guide, while Wipro TCV -45% YoY and falling deal sizes weigh on visibility.
Tier-1 margin fell 20bp YoY to 20.2% on AI investments, lateral hiring and wage hikes (Infosys, HCLT, Cyient, Zensar scheduled for 3Q-4Q); Coforge lifting its margin guide to 16% was rewarded.

price_drivers.driver: AI-led pricing deflation and deal-size compression
price_drivers.why: MOFSL notes deal sizes and durations are shrinking, pushing Tier-1 and Tier-2 into the same deals and compressing renewal pricing.
Rupee depreciation lifts INR margin while currency headwinds hurt some Tier-1 CC-to-USD conversion in 2Q.

kpis.name: Constant-currency revenue growth (QoQ and YoY, organic)
kpis.definition: Revenue growth with currency effects removed, stated organic where acquisitions contribute (Coforge 10.9% total vs 3.8% organic), by vertical and geography.
kpis.formula: reported CC growth (company); organic = CC growth less acquired revenue
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Sector multiples are set on CC growth relative to peers: the 2.3% median in 2QFY27 and Tier-2's 3.0% vs Tier-1's 1.2% explain relative P/E gaps; a guidance cut such as Infosys' second cut to (-0.5%) to 0.5% resets forward EPS.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation metric filter 'constant currency' for INFY, HCLTECH, WIPRO, TECHM, LTM, KPITTECH, LTTS, TATAELXSI, TATATECH (in the Airavat company list); get_financials for INR revenue; MOFSL results tables in the library carry 8 quarters of USD and CC growth for TCS and others.
kpis.estimate_source: get_consensus_estimates for Sales (INR) and EPS; USD growth derived with broker USD/INR; guidance bands from transcripts (get_qa for analyst Q&A); house live model at /sector/it-services for tier-1 drivers.
kpis.traps: Cross-currency effects and acquisitions distort headline growth; some firms report USD growth only; Wipro and others give guidance as a QoQ band not an annual number; INR growth is not CC growth.

kpis.name: EBIT margin and QoQ margin bridge
kpis.definition: Operating profit over revenue (EBIT, or EBITDA for ER&D) with a bridge for wage hike, INR, utilisation, pyramid, subcontracting and one-offs.
kpis.formula: EBIT / revenue from operations; bridge from company deck
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Tier-1 margin of 20.2% (-20bp YoY) and Tier-2 at 14.6% (flat) show that growth is being bought with AI investment and lateral hiring; each 100bp of EBIT is ~5% of EPS, and managements guiding range-bound margins through FY27 caps upside.
kpis.history_source: get_financials (employee cost, other expenses, D&A, EBIT); get_investor_presentation filters 'EBIT margin' and 'margin bridge'; transcripts for wage-hike timing and one-offs.
kpis.estimate_source: get_consensus_estimates gives EBITDA and EPS (Bloomberg); company margin guidance and bands in transcripts (Coforge 16% EBIT); live model at /sector/it-services; no consensus for EBIT margin itself.
kpis.traps: Other income FX gains and lower variable pay flatter EBIT; depreciation dips flatter margin; equipment and software pass-through lowers margin; M&A amortisation; margin defined as EBITDA for some ER&D names.

kpis.name: TCV, large deals and book-to-bill
kpis.definition: Total contract value of deals won in the quarter, LTM TCV, number of large deals and TCV divided by revenue.
kpis.formula: reported TCV; book-to-bill = quarterly TCV / quarterly revenue
kpis.why_it_moves_price: TCV leads revenue by 2-4 quarters; 2QFY27 TCV growth of +68% (Infosys), +27% (HCLT) and +102% (Coforge) against -45% (Wipro) and -12% (Mphasis) predicts the relative growth ranking and drives target-price revisions.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation metric filter 'TCV' and 'deal wins' (INFY, HCLTECH, WIPRO, TECHM, LTM decks); transcripts via search_research; MOFSL results notes in the library.
kpis.estimate_source: No consensus field for TCV; management commentary on pipeline and ramp in transcripts; broker models in the library.
kpis.traps: Not all firms disclose TCV (TCS gives deal wins only in calls; ER&D names often give none); TCV includes renewals and multi-year deals with slow ramps; deals announced but not yet booked.

kpis.name: FY27 revenue and margin guidance (band vs delivery)
kpis.definition: Management annual CC growth and margin guidance bands, tracked against each quarter's delivery and revisions.
kpis.formula: reported band; revision = change in band midpoint
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Guidance resets anchor forward EPS: Infosys' second cut to (-0.5%) to 0.5% CC is the key negative in the quarter, while HCLT's higher floor (2.5-4.0%), Coforge's margin raise to 16% and Mphasis' raise to low double digits drive the upgrades.
kpis.history_source: transcripts via search_research and get_qa with ticker and quarter filters; get_investor_presentation filter 'guidance'; MOFSL guidance sections in the library.
kpis.estimate_source: Company guidance in transcripts is the source; get_consensus_estimates shows whether Bloomberg Sales and EPS sit inside the band.
kpis.traps: Guidance is organic vs inorganic (HCLT raised on M&A) and by segment (IT services vs total); several companies guide only qualitatively; margin bands quoted on EBIT vs EBITDA.

kpis.name: Headcount, utilisation and revenue per employee
kpis.definition: Net headcount adds, fresher intake, utilisation and annualised USD revenue per employee.
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Net adds lead revenue by one quarter; utilisation and pyramid are the main margin levers management cites (higher utilisation and offshoring supported Tier-1 margins in 2Q), and subcontracting rising with flat adds means growth is being bought.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation filters 'headcount', 'utilisation' and 'subcontractor'; get_financials for employee cost; transcripts for hiring plans.
kpis.estimate_source: No consensus; management hiring guidance in transcripts and broker models.
kpis.traps: Headcount includes acquisitions and subcontractors differently; utilisation defined with or without trainees; ER&D utilisation includes ramp-down bench.

kpis.name: LTM attrition
kpis.definition: Voluntary attrition over the last twelve months as a percentage of average headcount.
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Rising attrition forces wage hikes and lateral hiring that MOFSL cites as margin offsets; Persistent, LTM, Tata Tech and Tata Elxsi hiked wages in 2Q and Infosys, HCLT, Cyient and Zensar follow in 3Q-4Q, so attrition predicts margin cost.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation metric filter 'attrition'; transcripts via search_research.
kpis.estimate_source: No consensus; management commentary in transcripts.
kpis.traps: LTM vs annualised quarterly; some firms exclude subsidiaries; lower variable pay can depress attrition temporarily.

kpis.name: Vertical and geography mix (BFSI, retail, manufacturing, hi-tech; Americas, Europe)
kpis.definition: Revenue growth and share by industry vertical and by geography, with BFSI and retail tracked separately.
kpis.formula: reported; vertical CC growth QoQ and YoY
kpis.why_it_moves_price: BFSI is the largest vertical for most large IT names and discretionary retail the swing vertical; vertical growth gaps explain why peers growing at the same headline rate carry different multiples.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation filter 'vertical' and 'geography'; get_financials segment note (filings can have fewer segments than the deck, e.g. TCS 6 vs 8 verticals).
kpis.estimate_source: No consensus by vertical; management commentary in transcripts and broker models.
kpis.traps: Vertical names differ across companies (Retail and CPG vs Consumer Business); filing segments and deck verticals must not be mixed; reclassifications.

kpis.name: INR/USD and currency mix (realised rates)
kpis.definition: Average realised USD/INR and the share of USD, GBP, EUR in revenue.
kpis.formula: reported realised rate; INR EBIT sensitivity per 1% move
kpis.why_it_moves_price: A 1% rupee depreciation adds ~20-30bp to IT services EBIT (higher for ER&D), so a 3% move is worth ~1-1.5% of EPS; GBP and EUR cross-currency shifts swing reported USD growth versus CC.
kpis.history_source: get_commodity_prices for INR:USD (spot and history); get_investor_presentation filters 'realised rate' and 'currency mix'.
kpis.estimate_source: Bloomberg forward INR via get_commodity_prices; house INR assumption in the live model at /sector/it-services; no consensus on currency mix.
kpis.traps: Hedge gains in other income; closing vs average rate; non-USD share above ~45% needs per-currency sensitivity.

kpis.name: ER&D client concentration and programme cycle
kpis.definition: Top-1, top-5 and top-10 client share of revenue, with vertical exposure to auto and programme ramps and roll-offs.
kpis.formula: reported; top client share = top client revenue / total revenue
kpis.why_it_moves_price: ER&D revenue follows client R&D budgets and vehicle programme cycles; a top client above ~20% of revenue means one OEM programme delay can cut growth for several quarters (Cyient, LTTS, KPIT and Tata Elxsi carried positive 2Q prints, so concentration is the next-quarter risk).
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation filters 'top client' and 'client concentration' for KPITTECH, LTTS, TATAELXSI, TATATECH; related-party filings for group-company clients; transcripts for programme timing.
kpis.estimate_source: No consensus; company deal and programme commentary in transcripts; broker models in the library.
kpis.traps: Top-client revenue is often not reported; group-company clients show only in related-party notes; pass-through and licence revenue is lumpy.

valuation_anchor: Forward P/E against each company's own 10-year band (IT services) with premium or discount to the nearest Tier-1 peer; ER&D names on 1-2 year forward P/E anchored on the post-2020 growth regime, with PEG, FCF and dividend yield as cross-checks.
watch_next_quarter: Per MOFSL, most managements expect margins to stay range-bound through FY27: track whether Infosys' FY27 guide of (-0.5%) to 0.5% CC holds, Tier-1 and Tier-2 TCV conversion as deal sizes shrink, wage hikes landing in 3Q-4Q (Infosys, HCLT, Cyient, Zensar, LTTS), and Coforge's USD2.4b order book converting to its 16% EBIT guide.
